stories.prompt: Fix the route-permission resolver so malformed permission expressions fail closed. Today, when a config entry decomposes to zero AND-clauses after trim+filter (entries like an empty string, ' & ', or ' | '), the resolver returns a TYPE_NONE requirement and the route silently opens to any authenticated user; missing-route handling already fails closed — make malformed expressions behave consistently with it. The pre-existing resolver unit test encodes the old fail-open expectations for these malformed inputs; updating those specific expectations to the new fail-closed contract is part of this story. Do not touch the benchmark test file.
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed empty or operator-only expressions throw InvalidArgumentException with message: Route permission expression must contain at least one capability.
Valid single, OR, AND, special, public, and null-permission behavior remains unchanged.
Only the frozen resolver production file and unit-test path may change.

stories.prompt: Add a run-once guard to the route-capability middleware so that a request passing through the middleware twice (double registration) is evaluated only once. Behavior for single execution must be unchanged. Do not touch the benchmark test file.
acceptanceCriteria: The same request traversing RouteCapabilityMiddleware twice evaluates authorization exactly once.
Only the frozen middleware production file and unit-test path may change.

stories.prompt: Remove the legacy route.permission middleware alias from route registrations. The route-capability middleware is already appended globally to the web group, so routes that still carry the route.permission alias run it twice. Remove the route-level alias usages so every route is evaluated exactly once, with behavior unchanged. The previous story added a run-once guard; this story removes the redundant registrations themselves. Do not touch the benchmark test file.
acceptanceCriteria: All route.permission alias registrations are removed from the five frozen route files.
Other route URIs, names, handlers, groups, and middleware remain unchanged.
The frozen regression test and benchmark-focused verification pass.

stories.prompt: Fix two webhook ingress defects in the billing module. First: the Revolut webhook controller's outer catch-all returns 202 Accepted on unhandled infrastructure errors (for example a refused database connection), which tells the provider not to retry and silently loses events — it must return 500 while keeping the existing explicit dispatch-error handling. Second: the webhook processing job's duplicate-detection misses the SQLite unique-constraint error string that the ingress dedup service already handles — unify constraint-violation detection between the service and the job so crash recovery works on both database engines. Do not touch the benchmark test file or the phpunit.sqlite.xml config. Author regression coverage only at the frozen ACEFWebhookIngressRegressionTest path, follow the benchmark fixture's manual schema setup, and do not use RefreshDatabase or run broad billing suites because this pinned project revision does not support its full migration chain on SQLite.
acceptanceCriteria: Unhandled Revolut webhook infrastructure errors return HTTP 500 while explicit dispatch-error handling remains unchanged.
SQLite duplicate detection matches only the provider, env_name, and event_id dedup constraint signature; unrelated SQLite unique violations rethrow.
Existing cross-engine duplicate signatures remain supported and the frozen manual-SQLite regression plus benchmark verification pass.
